passages.text: Then some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”
passages.sermon:
Some men came down from Judea.
These men taught the brothers.
They said, “You must be circumcised according to the custom of Moses.
If you are not circumcised, you cannot be saved.”
passages.original: Καί τινες κατελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐδίδασκον τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι Ἐὰν μὴ περιτμηθῆτε τῷ ἔθει τῷ Μωϋσέως οὐ δύνασθε σωθῆναι

passages.text: And after engaging these men in sharp debate, Paul and Barnabas were appointed, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas were Christian leaders and missionaries.
Some men from Judea taught that circumcision was necessary for salvation.
Paul and Barnabas strongly disagreed with these men.
They argued with them for a long time.
The church decided to send Paul and Barnabas to Jerusalem.
Some other believers went with them.
They went to meet the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.
They went to discuss this important question.
passages.original: γενομένης δὲ στάσεως καὶ ζητήσεως οὐκ ὀλίγης τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔταξαν ἀναβαίνειν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρνάβαν καί τινας ἄλλους ἐξ αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ πρεσβυτέρους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ τοῦ ζητήματος τούτου

passages.text: Sent on their way by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.
passages.sermon:
The church sent Paul, Barnabas, and some other believers on their way.
They traveled through Phoenicia.
They also traveled through Samaria.
They told people in these places how Gentiles had turned to God.
All the brothers heard this news.
This news brought great joy to all the brothers.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν προπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας διήρχοντο τήν τε Φοινίκην καὶ Σαμάρειαν ἐκδιηγούμενοι τὴν ἐπιστροφὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν καὶ ἐποίουν χαρὰν μεγάλην πᾶσιν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς

passages.text: On their arrival in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and apostles and elders, to whom they reported all that God had done through them.
passages.sermon:
Paul, Barnabas, and the other believers arrived in Jerusalem.
The church welcomed them.
The apostles welcomed them.
The elders welcomed them.
Paul, Barnabas, and the others told the church, apostles, and elders everything God had done through them.
passages.original: παραγενόμενοι δὲ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρεδέχθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἀνήγγειλάν τε ὅσα ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: But some believers from the party of the Pharisees stood up and declared, “The Gentiles must be circumcised and required to obey the law of Moses.”
passages.sermon:
Some believers belonged to the party of the Pharisees.
These believers had faith in Jesus.
They stood up among the people.
They spoke to the group.
They said, “The Gentiles must be circumcised.”
They also said, “We must command the Gentiles to obey the law of Moses.”
passages.original: Ἐξανέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς αἱρέσεως τῶν Φαρισαίων πεπιστευκότες λέγοντες ὅτι Δεῖ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς παραγγέλλειν τε τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως

passages.text: So the apostles and elders met to look into this matter.
passages.sermon: The apostles gathered together.\r\nThe elders gathered together.\r\nThey met to discuss this matter.
passages.original: Συνήχθησάν τε οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἰδεῖν περὶ τοῦ λόγου τούτου

passages.text: After much discussion, Peter got up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you that the Gentiles would hear from my lips the message of the gospel and believe.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle and a leader among the believers.
There was much discussion among the apostles and elders.
Peter stood up and spoke to them.
He said, “Brothers, you know this truth.
Long ago, God made a choice among you.
God chose that the Gentiles would hear the message of the gospel from my lips.
God wanted the Gentiles to believe.”
passages.original: Πολλῆς δὲ ζητήσεως γενομένης ἀναστὰς Πέτρος εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἀφ’ ἡμερῶν ἀρχαίων ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεὸς διὰ τοῦ στόματός μου ἀκοῦσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὸν λόγον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καὶ πιστεῦσαι

passages.text: And God, who knows the heart, showed His approval by giving the Holy Spirit to them, just as He did to us.
passages.sermon:
God knows every heart.
God showed His approval to the Gentiles.
God gave the Holy Spirit to the Gentiles.
God gave the Holy Spirit to us also.
God treated them and us the same way.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ καρδιογνώστης Θεὸς ἐμαρτύρησεν αὐτοῖς δοὺς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον καθὼς καὶ ἡμῖν

passages.text: He made no distinction between us and them, for He cleansed their hearts by faith.
passages.sermon:
God made no distinction between us and the Gentiles.
God saw us and the Gentiles as equal.
God cleansed their hearts by faith.
God used faith to purify their hearts.
God did this for the Gentiles just as He did for us.
passages.original: καὶ οὐθὲν διέκρινεν μεταξὺ ἡμῶν τε καὶ αὐτῶν τῇ πίστει καθαρίσας τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν

passages.text: Now then, why do you test God by placing on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear?
passages.sermon:
God is all-knowing and holy.
God gave the Holy Spirit to the Gentiles, just as He gave to us.
God made no distinction between us and them.
God cleansed their hearts by faith.
Now, you test God.
You try to put a heavy burden on the disciples.
This burden is like a yoke on their necks.
Neither our fathers nor we could carry this yoke.
Do not demand from the disciples what we ourselves could not bear.
passages.original: Νῦν οὖν τί πειράζετε τὸν Θεόν ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τῶν μαθητῶν ὃν οὔτε οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν οὔτε ἡμεῖς ἰσχύσαμεν βαστάσαι

passages.text: On the contrary, we believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.”
passages.sermon:
We believe in the Lord Jesus Christ.
We believe that He saves us by His grace.
He saves us in the same way that He saves them.
We are saved by grace, not by our own works.
They are also saved by grace, just as we are.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ πιστεύομεν σωθῆναι καθ’ ὃν τρόπον κἀκεῖνοι

passages.text: The whole assembly fell silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul describing the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
passages.sermon:
The whole assembly became silent.
Barnabas and Paul spoke to the assembly.
Barnabas and Paul described what God had done.
God had performed signs and wonders.
God did these signs and wonders among the Gentiles.
God did these things through Barnabas and Paul.
The assembly listened to Barnabas and Paul.
passages.original: Ἐσίγησεν δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος καὶ ἤκουον Βαρνάβα καὶ Παύλου ἐξηγουμένων ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν δι’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: When they had finished speaking, James declared, “Brothers, listen to me!
passages.sermon:
James was a leader in the early church.
James waited until Barnabas and Paul finished speaking.
James answered the assembly.
James said, "Brothers, listen to me."
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ σιγῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπεκρίθη Ἰάκωβος λέγων Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ἀκούσατέ μου

passages.text: Simon has told us how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people to be His own.
passages.sermon:
Simon spoke to the assembly.
Simon explained what God did first.
God visited the Gentiles.
God chose people from the Gentiles.
God made these people His own.
God called these people by His name.
passages.original: Συμεὼν ἐξηγήσατο καθὼς πρῶτον ὁ Θεὸς ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν λαὸν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written: ‘After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it, so that the remnant of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by My name, says the Lord who does these things that have been known for ages.’
passages.sermon:
The prophets spoke words from God.
Their words agree with what I have said.
God wrote these words long ago.
God said, “After this I will return.
I will rebuild the tent of David.
This tent has fallen down.
I will rebuild its ruins.
I will make it stand again.
Then the rest of the people will seek the Lord.
All the Gentiles will seek Me too.
These Gentiles are called by My name.
The Lord says this.
The Lord does these things.
He has made these things known from long ago.”
passages.original: καὶ τούτῳ συμφωνοῦσιν οἱ λόγοι τῶν προφητῶν καθὼς γέγραπται Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαυὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν καὶ τὰ κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν Κύριον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐφ’ οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπ’ αὐτούς λέγει Κύριος ποιῶν ταῦτα γνωστὰ ἀπ’ αἰῶνος

passages.text: It is my judgment, therefore, that we should not cause trouble for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
passages.sermon:
James is speaking to the church leaders in Jerusalem.
James gives his judgment.
James says, "We should not trouble the Gentiles."
The Gentiles are people from other nations.
These Gentiles are turning to God.
We should not make it hard for them.
passages.original: Διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
passages.sermon:
The apostles and elders gave instructions to the Gentile believers.
They told them to avoid food that idols have polluted.
They told them to avoid sexual immorality.
They told them to avoid meat from animals that people have strangled.
They told them to avoid blood.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ τοῦ πνικτοῦ καὶ τοῦ αἵματος

passages.text: For Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”
passages.sermon:
Moses is a key figure in the Jewish faith.
People have proclaimed the teachings of Moses in every city for many generations.
Leaders read the writings of Moses in the synagogues every Sabbath.
This public reading happens regularly each week.
passages.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων κατὰ πόλιν τοὺς κηρύσσοντας αὐτὸν ἔχει ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκόμενος

passages.text: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers, and sent them with this letter: The apostles and the elders, your brothers, To the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
passages.sermon:
The apostles and the elders led the early church in Jerusalem.
They met together with the whole church.
They decided to choose some men from among themselves.
They wanted to send these men to Antioch.
They sent them with Paul and Barnabas.
They chose Judas, who was called Barsabbas.
They also chose Silas.
Judas and Silas were leaders among the believers.
The apostles and elders wrote a letter.
They sent the letter by the hands of these men.
The letter was from the apostles and elders, who were brothers in Christ.
The letter was addressed to the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
The letter began with a greeting.
passages.original: Τότε ἔδοξε τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις σὺν ὅλῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐκλεξαμένους ἄνδρας ἐξ αὐτῶν πέμψαι εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν σὺν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ Βαρνάβᾳ Ἰούδαν τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν καὶ Σιλᾶν ἄνδρας ἡγουμένους ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς γράψαντες διὰ χειρὸς αὐτῶν Οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἀδελφοὶ Τοῖς κατὰ τὴν Ἀντιόχειαν καὶ Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἀδελφοῖς τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν Χαίρειν

passages.text: It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by what they said.
passages.sermon:
We heard about a problem.
Some men left us.
They did not have our permission.
They spoke to you.
Their words unsettled you.
They troubled your minds.
We did not tell them to do this.
passages.original: Ἐπειδὴ ἠκούσαμεν ὅτι τινὲς ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξελθόντες ἐτάραξαν ὑμᾶς λόγοις ἀνασκευάζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν οἷς οὐ διεστειλάμεθα

passages.text: So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
The apostles and elders are leaders in the early church.
They met together with the whole church.
They agreed together on a decision.
They chose certain men from among themselves.
They decided to send these men to you.
They sent these men with Barnabas and Paul.
Barnabas and Paul are beloved by the church.
Barnabas and Paul have risked their lives.
They risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ἔδοξεν ἡμῖν γενομένοις ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐκλεξαμένοις ἄνδρας πέμψαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς σὺν τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς ἡμῶν Βαρνάβᾳ καὶ Παύλῳ ἀνθρώποις παραδεδωκόσι τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to tell you in person the same things we are writing.
passages.sermon: We are sending Judas and Silas to you.\r\nJudas and Silas will speak to you in person.\r\nThey will tell you the same things we are writing in this letter.
passages.original: ἀπεστάλκαμεν οὖν Ἰούδαν καὶ Σιλᾶν καὶ αὐτοὺς διὰ λόγου ἀπαγγέλλοντας τὰ αὐτά

passages.text: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit guided us.
We also agreed with the Holy Spirit.
We decided not to give you any extra burdens.
We require only these necessary things.
You must not eat food offered to idols.
You must not eat blood.
You must not eat meat from animals that were strangled.
You must not practice sexual immorality.
If you keep away from these things, you will do well.
Goodbye.
passages.original: Ἔδοξεν γὰρ τῷ Πνεύματι τῷ Ἁγίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν μηδὲν πλέον ἐπιτίθεσθαι ὑμῖν βάρος πλὴν τούτων τῶν ἐπάναγκες ἀπέχεσθαι εἰδωλοθύτων καὶ αἵματος καὶ πνικτῶν καὶ πορνείας ἐξ ὧν διατηροῦντες ἑαυτοὺς εὖ πράξετε Ἔρρωσθε

passages.text: So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.
passages.sermon:
Judas and Silas were sent off by the church leaders in Jerusalem.
They traveled down to Antioch.
They gathered the whole congregation in Antioch.
They gave the letter to the people.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀπολυθέντες κατῆλθον εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν καὶ συναγαγόντες τὸ πλῆθος ἐπέδωκαν τὴν ἐπιστολήν

passages.text: When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.
passages.sermon: The people read the letter.\r\nThe letter gave encouragement.\r\nThe people rejoiced because of the encouragement.
passages.original: ἀναγνόντες δὲ ἐχάρησαν ἐπὶ τῇ παρακλήσει

passages.text: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
passages.sermon:
Judas and Silas were prophets.
They spoke to the brothers.
They said many things.
They encouraged the brothers.
They strengthened the brothers.
passages.original: Ἰούδας τε καὶ Σιλᾶς καὶ αὐτοὶ προφῆται ὄντες διὰ λόγου πολλοῦ παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐπεστήριξαν

passages.text: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to those who had sent them.
passages.sermon:
Judas and Silas were prophets.
\r\nThey stayed with the believers for some time.
\r\nThe brothers sent Judas and Silas off in peace.
\r\nJudas and Silas returned to those who had sent them.
passages.original: ποιήσαντες δὲ χρόνον ἀπελύθησαν μετ’ εἰρήνης ἀπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστείλαντας αὐτούς

passages.text: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch.
Many others stayed with them.
Paul and Barnabas taught the word of the Lord.
Paul and Barnabas preached the word of the Lord.
The others also taught and preached the word of the Lord.
passages.original: Παῦλος δὲ καὶ Βαρνάβας διέτριβον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι μετὰ καὶ ἑτέρων πολλῶν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle and a preacher of the word of the Lord.
Barnabas was his companion in ministry.
Some time passed.
Paul spoke to Barnabas.
Paul said, “Let us go back.”
Paul wanted to visit the brothers in every town.
These towns were the places where Paul and Barnabas had proclaimed the word of the Lord.
Paul wanted to see how the brothers were doing.
passages.original: Μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας εἶπεν πρὸς Βαρνάβαν Παῦλος Ἐπιστρέψαντες δὴ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς κατὰ πόλιν πᾶσαν ἐν αἷς κατηγγείλαμεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου πῶς ἔχουσιν

passages.text: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas was a Christian leader.
\r\nBarnabas wanted to take John with him.
\r\nPeople also called John by the name Mark.
passages.original: Βαρνάβας δὲ ἐβούλετο συμπαραλαβεῖν καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην τὸν καλούμενον Μάρκον

passages.text: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle and a leader in the early church.
Paul did not want to take John Mark with them.
John Mark had left them before in Pamphylia.
John Mark had not continued with them in the work.
Paul thought it was best not to bring John Mark.
passages.original: Παῦλος δὲ ἠξίου τὸν ἀποστάντα ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Παμφυλίας καὶ μὴ συνελθόντα αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἔργον μὴ συμπαραλαμβάνειν τοῦτον

passages.text: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus, but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas were Christian leaders and missionaries.
They had a strong disagreement.
The disagreement caused them to separate from each other.
Barnabas took Mark with him.
Barnabas sailed to Cyprus with Mark.
Paul chose Silas to go with him.
The brothers commended Paul to the grace of the Lord.
Paul left with Silas.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ παροξυσμός ὥστε ἀποχωρισθῆναι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων τόν τε Βαρνάβαν παραλαβόντα τὸν Μάρκον ἐκπλεῦσαι εἰς Κύπρον Παῦλος δὲ ἐπιλεξάμενος Σιλᾶν ἐξῆλθεν παραδοθεὶς τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν

passages.text: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
passages.sermon: Paul traveled through Syria.\r\nPaul also traveled through Cilicia.\r\nHe strengthened the churches in those regions.
passages.original: διήρχετο δὲ τὴν Συρίαν καὶ τὴν Κιλικίαν ἐπιστηρίζων τὰς ἐκκλησίας
